To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more a pattern is used to support the system purpose, the more it changes and the more resilient to changes it becomes.

(i) the evolution of design pattern is strongly influenced by their purpose, (ii) the changes that a pattern undergoes are strongly influenced by its purpose, and (iii) the impact of changes on co-changed code and the ability to make the system resilient to the change are strongly influenced by the kind of change.

(1) design patterns change more often in systems that are less stable and that are not well designed, and (2) design patterns are more resilient to changes when they are used to solve problems that are more specific to the application domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the factors that influence design patterns evolution, with the goal to help developers in their decision of which patterns to use, and how to use them.
providing a better understanding of design patterns evolution and its impact on the evolution of systems.

understanding the evolution of a specific kind of design artifact and its impact on the system as a whole, in order to provide better guidelines to the developers for the maintenance of design patterns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of design pattern is a complex phenomenon, and that the study of this phenomenon is still in its infancy.
the more the pattern is suited to the application purpose, the more it is modified, the less the impact of changes on co-changed code, the more the capability of making the code resilient to changes.
the more frequently a pattern is used the more it evolves, and that the more it evolves the more its co-changed classes evolve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patterns evolve in the same way as the system evolves, and that this evolution is strongly influenced by the application domain.
design patterns are not static entities, but they evolve along with their context.
the more frequently the patterns are modified, the more they tend to change their structure and the less they tend to change the classes they affect, thus becoming more resilient to changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to improve the maintainability of a system, it is important to understand how design patterns are used in the code base.
the evolution of design pattern can be effectively used as a proxy to assess the evolution of the system design.
the evolution of a design pattern should not be considered in isolation from the evolution of the system in which it is embedded.
